name: Cascade Residential Trust
description: Public multifamily REIT with an existing Sun Belt garden/mid-rise portfolio, actively acquiring to densify Southeast markets.
notes: Owns assets in 3 of the 6 target submarkets already; stated 2024-2025 growth guidance is Southeast-weighted.

name: Bluepoint Residential Partners
description: Public multifamily REIT, national footprint, opportunistic bolt-on M&A strategy, has done 2 portfolio acquisitions of similar size in the past 3 years.
notes: Track record of similar-sized platform deals, but Atlanta is a new-to-market expansion rather than an infill.

name: Harborline Apartment REIT
description: Public multifamily REIT, core strategy, lower leverage tolerance, prioritizes gateway and large Sun Belt metros.
notes: Would likely underwrite the Class B/B+ assets below their typical quality bar; slower decision process.

name: Ridgemont Living
description: Private regional multifamily operator based in the Southeast, actively rolling up garden-style communities via a programmatic acquisition vehicle.
notes: Direct competitor/adjacent operator in the same submarkets; would run the platform, not just the assets.

name: Meridian Community Group
description: Private Southeast multifamily platform backed by a family office, seeking scale via M&A rather than one-off deals.
notes: Explicitly stated intent to add 2,500-4,000 units via acquisition over the next 18 months.

name: Northgate Real Estate Capital
description: Value-add-focused private equity real estate fund, Sun Belt multifamily specialist, typically holds 4-6 years.
notes: Fund has significant dry powder earmarked for Sun Belt multifamily; comfortable with the Class B/B+ mix and light value-add story.

name: Anchor Point Realty Advisors
description: Institutional separate account manager investing on behalf of pension and insurance capital, core-plus mandate, national.
notes: Core-plus mandate is a stretch fit for the below-average-occupancy assets without a stabilization plan.

name: Silverleaf Capital Partners
description: Opportunistic private equity real estate fund targeting mispriced or under-managed multifamily portfolios.
notes: Underwriting appetite for the lower-occupancy assets (East Point, Kennesaw, Marietta) fits their thesis well.

name: Highland Pension Real Estate
description: Direct real estate investment arm of a public pension fund, core mandate, very long hold periods, low leverage.
notes: Core mandate and long hold period are a mismatch for a portfolio with meaningful lease-up / occupancy ramp still ahead of it.

name: Foundry Street Partners
description: Middle-market private equity real estate fund specializing in growth capital and recapitalizations for regional operating platforms.
notes: Also a credible counterparty for a recap/growth-capital structure rather than a full sale, per the dual-track consideration.
